findings.quote: In asexual reproduction, such as a bacterium splitting in two, one parent passes its DNA to its offspring with no gametes.
findings.problem: Boundary test fails. The sentence states, for asexual reproduction in general, that no gametes are involved. Parthenogenesis is a form of asexual reproduction in which an unfertilized egg, a gamete, develops into the offspring (for example honeybee drones). A student taught that asexual means no gametes can misclassify parthenogenesis as sexual reproduction. The round-1 fix replaced one false absolute (alleles pass only through gametes) with its opposite. The limit that holds is that no gametes fuse, which is how the branch lesson characteristics-of-life words it.
findings.source: Reader rules, Added after the Sol audit (boundary test); checklist B01; OpenStax Biology 2e, 43.1 Reproduction Methods (parthenogenesis is a form of asexual reproduction where an egg develops into a complete individual without being fertilized); branch lesson characteristics-of-life line 32 (no gametes fuse)

findings.quote: Variants arise by chance. Which ones spread depends on the present environment.
findings.problem: False as a general statement, and it contradicts the lesson's own teaching. Under genetic drift the variant that spreads is decided by chance, not by how well it fits the environment: Example #4 has the brown allele rise from 0.30 to 0.60 although being brown did not help survival. Under gene flow (Example #5) the green allele spreads on the island because pollen and seeds arrive. Trap #2, just above, warns that selection is not the only cause. Only selection makes spread depend on the environment. The base wrote this as which traits are favored, which is true; the rewrite widened it to which variants spread.
findings.source: Reader rules, Added after the Sol audit (boundary test); checklist B01; lesson Example #4, Example #5 and Trap #2; OpenStax Biology 2e, 19.2 Population Genetics (genetic drift changes allele frequencies by chance)

findings.quote: Chance in a small group points to drift.
findings.problem: This paragraph has four sentences, over the one-to-three limit. Still open from rounds 1 and 2 in other teaching paragraphs with four sentences: the gamete paragraph, the nonrandom mating paragraph, the first mutation paragraph, the comparing-causes paragraph, the species paragraph, the reproductive isolation paragraph, the sympatric speciation paragraph and the adaptive radiation paragraph.
findings.source: Checklist L22a; LSG Formatting rules (paragraphs of one to three short sentences); round-2 L22a finding
